variants.title: Half-life of indium-116m
variants.sample: Indium foil activated in a neutron howitzer (In-116m)
variants.note: A thin indium foil is activated by slow neutrons and counted as it decays. Its half-life of about 54 minutes is long enough to take many readings and short enough to finish in one laboratory session.

source.title: NNDC / IAEA evaluated nuclear data: In-116m half-life 54.29 min

variants.title: Half-life of barium-137m
variants.sample: Barium-137m eluted from a caesium-137 generator
variants.note: The isotope generator holds Cs-137, which decays to the excited state Ba-137m; a few drops of eluent wash the barium out and it decays with a half-life of about two and a half minutes, so the whole run takes a quarter of an hour.

source.title: NNDC / IAEA evaluated nuclear data: Ba-137m half-life 2.552 min, 661.7 keV gamma

variants.title: Half-life of protactinium-234m
variants.sample: Protactinium-234m separated from a uranyl salt solution
variants.note: The classic school version: protactinium is shaken out of a uranyl nitrate solution into a solvent layer and counted through the bottle. Its half-life is just over a minute, so the counts have to be short and quick.

source.title: NNDC / IAEA evaluated nuclear data: Pa-234m half-life 1.159 min
